control: Record the affected tenant, site, endpoint group, ring, operating-system scope, and update reference
State the technical or business reason the update cannot follow the normal deployment schedule
Attach the original scan, applicability result, failure code, compatibility evidence, or change constraint
Count every affected endpoint and reconcile the count to the current inventory source
Confirm whether internet-facing, privileged, executive, regulated, or otherwise high-impact devices are included
Document the update severity, known exploitation status, exposed service, and likely business impact
Assign a named risk owner who can accept, reject, or narrow the exception
Set an explicit start date and expiry date; do not approve an open-ended exception
Define temporary compensating controls such as service restriction, segmentation, allowlisting, enhanced logging, or user guidance
Verify that each compensating control is active on the full affected scope and retain evidence
Obtain approval from the exception owner and the customer or internal authority required by policy
Link the approved exception to the ticket, change record, policy, and affected endpoint records
Create a monitoring signal for scope drift, new exposure, exploitation evidence, failed controls, and approaching expiry
Set a review cadence proportionate to risk and assign the next review date
Define the safe retest method, pilot group, maintenance window, success criteria, and rollback trigger
Record each retest result, final endpoint state, reboot state, and unresolved failure reason
Deploy or otherwise remediate the update across the reconciled scope and retain post-action scan evidence
Remove temporary compensating controls when appropriate, close the exception, and record lessons or policy changes
